Sentence (English): One year in I'm still scratching my head as to how I paid so much for a dishwasher that doesn't dry your dishes.
Comments (English): [ Includes free imaginary dryer and soap flavor ] || ---------------- || One year in I'm still scratching my head as to how I paid so much for a dishwasher that doesn't dry your dishes. I should have looked into this a bit better as I was mislead by the \"Auto Dry\" marketing. \"Auto Dry\" just opens the door when its done, and in five or ten hours most your stuff is usually mostly dry unless it's plastic, and in that case it's still completely wet. This is fine when running it at the end of the day, but if you need to do a quick run and get the dishes out quick, you're stuck hand drying everything like it's Little House on the Prairie. It's nice how this is quiet, but yeah, not thrilled with how the business suits at Bosch are misleading people by labeling the \"open door when done\" button like it controls some non-existent dryer. They've definitely lost some trust with me. I also wish it would use a little more water when rinsing. Nearly everything comes out tasting of soap unless you put about 1/3 of the recommended soap in the wash, and still, I'm finding myself rinsing most of the dishes by hand before eating. Yes I'm using rinse-aid. This brings me back to the \"Auto Dry\" feature which you can't activate if you choose any cycles but the full wash. Also after choosing your options, it's impossible enable \"Auto Dry\" unless you do a hard reset, which is insanely stupid.

Sentence (English): While the customer service people I have dealt with have been friendly, our overall experience has been an absolute nightmare.
Comments (English): While the customer service people I have dealt with have been friendly, our overall experience has been an absolute nightmare. We ordered this dishwasher during Black Friday since there were many deals going on. We could have ordered from anyone, but chose Costco for the free installation and haul away, as this seemed like the easiest option. Boy were we wrong. The dishwasher was "delivered" a couple weeks after purchase, and from there on out our experience has gone way down hill. We have had the same installation company come 4 times, and still do not have an installed dishwasher. 1. The first 2 installers showed up and were very young--looked 18 years or younger and did not speak English. We walked over to the sink and they pointed at me and my boyfriend and under the sink. We finally determined that they were asking us to go under our sink and shut our water off. Us being confused as that is why we hired them, we got down there and tried since they clearly were not going to do it. We weren't really sure what we were doing, and definitely were not qualified to do it. They were trying to communicate with us via Google Translate, but we still were not understanding what was going on. Finally, they called their manager and he told us that our pipes were corroded and that we needed to refuse the dishwasher because they could not install it. This was definitely not true but we were getting nowhere given the language barriers so we did what we were told and they left with the dishwasher. Costco followed up via phone and reviewed the photos that were shared and assured us that our pipes were not corroded and apologized for the poor experience. They said they would send more experienced installers to come. I asked if there was anything I needed to do beforehand so that we would not run into issues again. The assured me that I did not. 2. Our dishwasher got rescheduled for 1 week later. They arrived and did not have the dishwasher because they were under the impression that it was left here, even though I confirmed on 2 separate Costco phone calls that we did not have the dishwasher and it was returned. I am also not sure how the installation company did not have any notes on this. When we talked to Costco again, they didn't even know where the dishwasher was and had to make phone calls to find it. 3. The 3rd installers came and it was 2 men who were very friendly and seemed experienced. They went to turn the valve to shut the water off to the dishwasher and said they could not attempt any further as they were worried the pipes would burst. The installer mentioned he had an extra valve and would replace it for us, but we would need to shut the water off in the whole unit (we live in a shared Condo/Apt Complex). We weren't sure how to do this and were not able to get ahold of anyone while they were here, so we had them leave. They mentioned once we figured out how to turn the water off to the unit, to let them know and they would bump us up in the schedule and get this resolved immediately (replace valve and install dishwasher). They also left the dishwasher this time so we would not run into that again. 4. Feeling not so confident, we rescheduled our 4th installation. When they called to confirm, they said “It's for an inspection right” and we explained no, we need our dishwasher installed and our valve replaced, which your company told us you would do. When they arrived they again asked if they were doing an inspection and we had to explain our situation AGAIN. They seemed very confused/not confident and told us they could not replace the valve even though it really should not be a difficult task and the previous installer from their company made it no big deal. I told them it was fine and we would shut off the water to the whole apartment so that they could install the dishwasher. They said per company policy, they could not do this and the valve would need to be replaced by a plumber, even though having the water shut off should have allowed them to install the dishwasher. They left, and now we are about 1 month in and 4 failed installations. We have been told a different thing each time the installers have come and at this point have little confidence. I've talked to Costco Customer service after every failed attempt and each time all I'm told is they can compensate us $75, which honestly feels minimal for the time we have wasted with the installers, prepping for them to come, and all the time spent on the phone with Customer Service. One of the Costco Customer Service Members I spoke to even blamed me and said it was our fault! If you choose Costco for your dishwasher, good luck.

We could have ordered from anyone, but chose Costco for the free installation and haul away, as this seemed like the easiest option. Boy were we wrong. The dishwasher was "delivered" a couple weeks after purchase, and from there on out our experience has gone way down hill. We have had the same installation company come 4 times, and still do not have an installed dishwasher. 1. The first 2 installers showed up and were very young--looked 18 years or younger and did not speak English. We walked over to the sink and they pointed at me and my boyfriend and under the sink. We finally determined that they were asking us to go under our sink and shut our water off. Us being confused as that is why we hired them, we got down there and tried since they clearly were not going to do it. We weren't really sure what we were doing, and definitely were not qualified to do it. They were trying to communicate with us via Google Translate, but we still were not understanding what was going on. Finally, they called their manager and he told us that our pipes were corroded and that we needed to refuse the dishwasher because they could not install it. This was definitely not true but we were getting nowhere given the language barriers so we did what we were told and they left with the dishwasher. Costco followed up via phone and reviewed the photos that were shared and assured us that our pipes were not corroded and apologized for the poor experience. They said they would send more experienced installers to come. I asked if there was anything I needed to do beforehand so that we would not run into issues again. The assured me that I did not. 2. Our dishwasher got rescheduled for 1 week later. They arrived and did not have the dishwasher because they were under the impression that it was left here, even though I confirmed on 2 separate Costco phone calls that we did not have the dishwasher and it was returned. I am also not sure how the installation company did not have any notes on this. When we talked to Costco again, they didn't even know where the dishwasher was and had to make phone calls to find it. 3. The 3rd installers came and it was 2 men who were very friendly and seemed experienced. They went to turn the valve to shut the water off to the dishwasher and said they could not attempt any further as they were worried the pipes would burst. The installer mentioned he had an extra valve and would replace it for us, but we would need to shut the water off in the whole unit (we live in a shared Condo/Apt Complex). We weren't sure how to do this and were not able to get ahold of anyone while they were here, so we had them leave. They mentioned once we figured out how to turn the water off to the unit, to let them know and they would bump us up in the schedule and get this resolved immediately (replace valve and install dishwasher). They also left the dishwasher this time so we would not run into that again. 4. Feeling not so confident, we rescheduled our 4th installation. When they called to confirm, they said “It's for an inspection right” and we explained no, we need our dishwasher installed and our valve replaced, which your company told us you would do. When they arrived they again asked if they were doing an inspection and we had to explain our situation AGAIN. They seemed very confused/not confident and told us they could not replace the valve even though it really should not be a difficult task and the previous installer from their company made it no big deal. I told them it was fine and we would shut off the water to the whole apartment so that they could install the dishwasher. They said per company policy, they could not do this and the valve would need to be replaced by a plumber, even though having the water shut off should have allowed them to install the dishwasher. They left, and now we are about 1 month in and 4 failed installations. We have been told a different thing each time the installers have come and at this point have little confidence. I've talked to Costco Customer service after every failed attempt and each time all I'm told is they can compensate us $75, which honestly feels minimal for the time we have wasted with the installers, prepping for them to come, and all the time spent on the phone with Customer Service. One of the Costco Customer Service Members I spoke to even blamed me and said it was our fault! If you choose Costco for your dishwasher, good luck.

Sentence (English): One year in I'm still scratching my head as to how I paid so much for a dishwasher that doesn't dry your dishes.
Comments (English): [ Includes free imaginary dryer and soap flavor ] || ---------------- || One year in I'm still scratching my head as to how I paid so much for a dishwasher that doesn't dry your dishes. I should have looked into this a bit better as I was mislead by the "Auto Dry" marketing. "Auto Dry" just opens the door when its done, and in five or ten hours most your stuff is usually mostly dry unless it's plastic, and in that case it's still completely wet. This is fine when running it at the end of the day, but if you need to do a quick run and get the dishes out quick, you're stuck hand drying everything like it's Little House on the Prairie. It's nice how this is quiet, but yeah, not thrilled with how the business suits at Bosch are misleading people by labeling the "open door when done" button like it controls some non-existent dryer. They've definitely lost some trust with me.I also wish it would use a little more water when rinsing. Nearly everything comes out tasting of soap unless you put about 1/3 of the recommended soap in the wash, and still, I'm finding myself rinsing most of the dishes by hand before eating. Yes I'm using rinse-aid.This brings me back to the "Auto Dry" feature which you can't activate if you choose any cycles but the full wash. Also after choosing your options, it's impossible enable "Auto Dry" unless you do a hard reset, which is insanely stupid.

Good thing they have the little red light that shines on your floor when it's running. We also set up and use its WiFi features; at first I thought, 'who the heck needs WiFi in a dishwasher?!' But it's useful, matter-of-fact.If you're reading reviews to make a buying decision, I really recommend our dishwasher. But my best advice would be to decide which features you truly need, and then go for the model that has 'em. I think you'll be happy with any Bosch model you pick, and you can save more than a few bucks by selecting a model with features that meet your needs. For example, the 800 series is wonderful, but if a 400 series will get the job done for you, go for one of those.

Sentence (English): I've been using it for about a month now, so I'm leaving a review.
Comments (English): I've been using it for about a month now, so I'm leaving a review. Initially, I was a little annoyed when it arrived broken, and I had to wait a full week (even over the weekend) to get a new one. However, the installers were friendly and quick, which quickly eased my frustration. First of all, the product is one level below the highest-end model. This one comes with a frying pan holder. Honestly, I didn't need that, so this was perfect. We have a family of five, and the largest pot you see in the photo fits. On days when I have the flu or a sick child, I use the hot air dryer. I don't need the steam feature, so I haven't tried it yet. And the pause feature is a godsend! When there are a lot of people, I leave it running and turn around to find cups scattered everywhere. Just pressing pause and putting them back in is perfect. I only wipe the coated pans separately and then put everything back in, which is a relief. Sentence (English): There are a lot of reasons one could like this machine.
Comments (English): [ Operates fine but I don't like it ] || ---------------- || There are a lot of reasons one could like this machine. It has a large capacity, it gets the dishes clean, it is quiet. But the industry trend of putting the controls and indicators on the top edge of the door where no one can see them while the machine is operating is, well, stupid. Making some features acessible only through a mobile phone app interface is lazy and rude to your customers. I'm standing literally within arms reach of the machine and I am expected to pull out my phone and open an app to see, just as an example, how much time is remaining on the cycle? When the cycle is finished and the red dot on the floor goes away, how does anyone else know by looking if the contents are dirty or clean? So many shortcomings that would have been solved by putting the controls on the front where they belong, and having adequate indicators not just during the cycle but afterward. I simply cannot be induced to like such a design or to recommend it to anyone else.

Sentence (English): We're extremely happy with our new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Best Dishwasher We've Ever Owned! ] || ---------------- || We're extremely happy with our new dishwasher. Its many features are amazing, but are easy to use and set up. The manual is also very good, so be sure to read it thoroughly to maximize on the dishwasher's features. We read the Consumer Reports article about Bosch dishwashers in general, which was about the fact that most of the Bosch models end up at the top of their ratings. So we made our Bosch decision based on that Consumer Reports article. We were totally unknowledgeable about the latest-and-greatest in dishwashers, so the research really paid off. We've had it just long enough to try all the washing cycles, and it does an amazing cleaning job. Our old one worked fine, but never cleaned the dishes and utensils as well, and as gently, as this one does. Our old one was 12 years old, so we figured it's time, anyway. Our model has the built-in water softening system, which we probably didn't need as we have a whole-house water softening system (so I've turned the feature off on the dishwasher). So if that's your situation, you can probably save more than a few bucks by getting a model that doesn't have it. As I'm sure others have commented, its quietness is amazing. Good thing they have the little red light that shines on your floor when it's running. We also set up and use its WiFi features; at first I thought, "who the heck needs WiFi in a dishwasher? " But it's useful, matter-of-fact. If you're reading reviews to make a buying decision, I really recommend our dishwasher. But my best advice would be to decide which features you truly need, and then go for the model that has 'em. I think you'll be happy with any Bosch model you pick, and you can save more than a few bucks by selecting a model with features that meet your needs. For example, the 800 series is wonderful, but if a 400 series will get the job done for you, go for one of those.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher as part of appliance set, and it was replacing a 7 year old dishwasher (other brand) that I was perfectly happy with.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher, except for lower rack tines. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher as part of appliance set, and it was replacing a 7 year old dishwasher (other brand) that I was perfectly happy with. The first thing I noticed is that the tines of the lower rack weretoo short and spaced too far apart. My bowls are broad and shallow, and they would lean over very far and knock against each other, leading to possible chipping. I had to space them in every other row to avoid knocking, and this cut way down on the amount of dishes i could load on the lower rack. The user's guide mentioned moveable bowl tines which could be adjusted so that bowls and other dishes would stand up straighter. I called customer service to enquire if I was supposed to have this, and if not, could I buy them. I was told that it did not come on this model (at over $1000 list price, the bottom of the KitchenAid line), and they were not available for purchase. I went back to the store to see the tines on an upgrade model, and they seemed adequate for the problem at hand. I called customer service again, and gave them the upgrade model number, and asked if I could buy them for my model. It was available by special order for $107, meaning I would have to pay in advance, no refunds, and no guarantee it woould fit my model. Plus I would have to buy 4 tine clips at $20 apiece, plus tax, shipping, and handling. so over $200 all together. I asked about just buying the lower rack of the upgrade model, and was told no, it wouldn't fit, because all KitchenAid dishwashers are different.So my advice is, if you have deep, coconut-shaped bowls, this model might be perfectly fine for you. But if you have wide, shallow bowls, look at the upgrade models first before purchasing.That being said, the dishwasher does a fine job of cleaning the dishes. After 3 weeks, I've had no food left on any dish, even the flatware and small items placed on the third rack, and no water spotting. At 39 dB, it's very quiet, although it can be louder depending on dishes and how their arranged. Also, this quiet mode is only for the normal wash cycle. Other cycles can be louder by 10 to 15 dB (my measurements). It also has an extended drying cycle option which helps with plastic items that don't dry as well. It has a small LED light on the front that glows blue during the wash cycle, red during drying mode, and white when complete. I really have no complaints about this model other than the tines of the bottom rack.

Comments (English): [ Suriprised by how quiet it is ] || ---------------- || We had a Frigidaire Professional Series dishwasher for a while. It served its purpose and was doing everything a dishwasher should do, until one day it decided that it did not want to do dirty dishes anymore. Long story short, we got Bosch Stainless 800 Series. Controls: easy to navigate, on the top of the door. One minor gripe - you cannot see time left, unless you open the door (stop the cycle). Top level model projects the number to the floor, but common, it is not a TV. Wash quality: very good. We noticed that the very top rack does not dry up as well, so our "stainless" steak knives started showing some rusting. Lesson learned - into the lower basket they go.Noise level: standing next to the working machine you would not know it is working.Overall: very happy. Hope it lasts as long as the Frigidaire did (15 years, daily use)

Comments (English): [ A mixed bag. Good performance, Poor design choices ] || ---------------- || I'd give it 3.5 stars if I could. The good: the oven cook very evenly, unlike our prior one. Having a built-in Air Fryer capability is nice, although compared to our countertop unit we need to set the temperature about 50 degrees higher to get the same amount of crisp. The neutral: The burners seem to take longer to heat up than our prior range, and I wish at least one of the rear burners was larger. The unit needs a large air space behind it, which pushes the front of the range far beyond the front of the cabinets next to it. The not-so-good: Ergonomically, it's kind of a mess. The black on chrome lettering on the knobs is very hard to read, and the tiny icons to indicate whether you're using the small, medium or large burner elements are almost impossible to see. And the surface of the rangetop seems fragile. Our prior range was at least 8 years old, and the cooktop was pretty much like new. The LG is already showing some marks that won't posligh out after only a couple of weeks. I expected better. Oh, and why do you include the basket for air frying, but not the rack the basket fits in? And why, if I choose to buy the rack, do I also have to get another basket? The rack should be included. At a minimum, it should be a cheap accessory that doesn't come with a second basket.

Reason for Purchase: I had been using a 12-place setting dishwasher from another brand since 2018 and was very satisfied with it, but I had to buy a new one due to moving. I use it more than once a day because it is so convenient. Since I am moving to a rental property where I will only be staying for two years, I was hesitant to buy a built-in model. I debated between the 12-place and 6-place settings and ultimately purchased the 6-place model. Since I do not own the property, I wanted to choose a 6-place setting that doesn't require drilling or cutting baseboards. However, there weren't as many products as I expected, so I chose a Samsung product because I could trust their after-sales service. 2. Product Pros and Cons: 1) Spacious Interior: I was used to the 12-place setting and wondered if the 6-place setting might be too small. However, the interior is wider than I expected, which is great. Of course, it holds less than the upper and lower compartments of the 12-place setting, but because it is deep, it is possible to wash a larger volume of dishes than I anticipated. I feel it is about 60% the size of the 12-place setting, not half. As a family of three, it is sufficient for simple morning dishwashing, and even for dinner, if the dishes aren't too deep... However, this product doesn't require any of that, so installation is simple. I gave up on a 12-place setting when moving, and the removal and reinstallation costs were in the mid-to-late 100,000 won range. I decided to add a little more money and buy a new one, and I think I made the right decision. Occasionally, those whose sinks do not have holes may need them, so please check before purchasing. Nowadays, apartment sinks have holes for things like detergent dispensers, but this one might not, so checking before installation is necessary. 3) Automatic door opening. This is a feature that anyone who has used a dishwasher will consider essential. Unless the dishwasher comes out completely dried with hot air... It is absolutely necessary because if it doesn't open, you have to open it manually every time. 4) Cons. I haven't really noticed any major issues and am using it well. 3. Overall Review. For those looking for a dishwasher of a suitable size that can be installed without drilling due to structural reasons or because it is not their own home, I recommend the Samsung dishwasher over the really cheap ones. Considering that it is easy to get after-sales service for defects, breakdowns, or moving, I think it offers great value for money. It is suitable for households of 2-3 people or those who do not cook every day.

For those looking for a dishwasher of a suitable size that can be installed without drilling due to structural reasons or because it is not their own home, I recommend the Samsung dishwasher over the really cheap ones. Considering that it is easy to get after-sales service for defects, breakdowns, or moving, I think it offers great value for money. It is suitable for households of 2-3 people or those who do not cook every day.

Sentence (English): Wanted to replace an older dishwasher that was horribly noisy.
Comments (English): [ Very quiet and spacious ] || ---------------- || Wanted to replace an older dishwasher that was horribly noisy. Looked into the Bosch brand for the good reviews. Arrived as scheduled. We are amazed at how quiet this dishwasher is! It's very spacious and we find that rack organization far better than our old one. The 3rd rack is great for cutlery so we've taken the cutlery basket out which provides even more room in the lower rack. Can easily put it back in of we need it. My one complaint is that the water line elbow adapter is not included (but necessary) when installing the dishwasher. For less than $10, why not just include it? For the premium price of the dishwasher, I would've expected that it would be. Simple enough to go to a hardware store but such a pain to do that when I wasn't expecting it. Otherwise, very pleased with the product.

Sentence (English): We had a Frigidaire Professional Series dishwasher for a while.
Comments (English): [ Suriprised by how quiet it is ] || ---------------- || We had a Frigidaire Professional Series dishwasher for a while. It served its purpose and was doing everything a dishwasher should do, until one day it decided that it did not want to do dirty dishes anymore. Long story short, we got Bosch Stainless 800 Series. Controls: easy to navigate, on the top of the door. One minor gripe - you cannot see time left, unless you open the door (stop the cycle). Top level model projects the number to the floor, but common, it is not a TV. Wash quality: very good. We noticed that the very top rack does not dry up as well, so our "stainless" steak knives started showing some rusting. Lesson learned - into the lower basket they go. Noise level: standing next to the working machine you would not know it is working. Overall: very happy. Hope it lasts as long as the Frigidaire did (15 years, daily use)

Sentence (English): Our smelly old 15+ year old dishwasher finally conked out and I decided to buy a Bosch.
Comments (English): [ A whole new world ] || ---------------- || Our smelly old 15+ year old dishwasher finally conked out and I decided to buy a Bosch. Having never before had a "modern" dishwasher, it's a whole new world -- and we love it. The overall design seems informed but how users actually use a dishwasher, and it addresses shortcomings of previous generations. The third rack on top is amazing and provides a ton of room for utensils. The middle rack pulls out easily and is tall enough to accommodate tall glasses. The bott rack has an open layout that allows it to accommodate all different kinds of dishes, and the tines are angled in a way that works equally well for plates or bowls and enables them to be stacked close together while also cleaning each one well. You can also wash cutting boards without having them scrape against the upper rack. The cleaning quality is good and the drying feature works better than any other dishwasher -- unless there's a divot that retains water, the dish will come out dry. I like being able to use the app as well.

Comments (English): We purchased a new dishwasher and extra parts along with the installation on 11/24/23. (Order # WJ********) We were given a delivery date of 12/2/2023. I called customer service to find out about the installation and was told the delivery guys also do the install. All would be taken care of by them. The morning of December 2, 2023 found two delivery men hauling our new dishwasher into the house. We had already pulled the old one out since that would make their job easier. The both said that they could handle 'easy' installations but the granite countertop and the copper tubing going across the bottom kept them from doing the installation. They said we needed a plumber and an electrician to redo the space since the new dishwasher sat flush on the floor. They told me that we would receive a phone call later that day from a 419 area code. I asked if that was in Toledo and they said it was. At 4:00pm I called customer service. Your representative was able to find our order but unable to find anything about the delivery or an update from your delivery guys. They repeatedly called the delivery company and the Toledo office but apparently no one was picking up. We gave up after 40 minutes. I tried customer service a couple of times over the weekend only to find computer systems had not yet been updated with our delivery information. On Monday 12/4/23 I reached out again to customer service and was rewarded. As a funny aside, I asked why it took so long for their computer systems to be updated or why the delivery guys or the Toledo office couldn't be reached on 12/2. He informed me that in his notes it stated there was an earthquake in Toledo as the reason no one could be reached or updated. Really? Your representative informed me that our install was scheduled for 12/12. They would call the day before to give us our four hour arrival window. They would also call again on the 12th when leaving their previous install and were on their way to us. I explained that it was important to have a plumber and an electrician included in the install team. I was assured that the Toledo installation teams could handle this and anything else thrown at them. “In my experience, these installations guys are successful 100% of time.” Everything worked according to plan and when the two install guys showed up, they looked at the new dishwasher; looked at the space and said “We can't do this type of install. You need to call a plumber.” My reaction was to laugh at sheer absurdity of this entire process but that response was muted as my wife just unloaded on the two of them. I think each were amazed about the sheer volume and length of the diatribe now directed at them about her 'new' dishwasher. There may have even been some raw language used which was definitely out of character. One of the guys got down on his knees, peered into the space and said, “It think I have an idea.” I retreated to my office as my wife was now in charge. It took maybe 45 minutes for them to get the new unit installed and running and those gentleman handled all the adversity quite well. At least they understood “always make the customer satisfied.” But my wife is still upset by the entire experience…. And the daily reminder that the dishwasher is crooked. It's not in line with everything else in the kitchen. …and we're still waiting to receive the missing kick plate from Samsung. It works.

I called customer service to find out about the installation and was told the delivery guys also do the install. All would be taken care of by them. The morning of December 2, 2023 found two delivery men hauling our new dishwasher into the house. We had already pulled the old one out since that would make their job easier. The both said that they could handle 'easy' installations but the granite countertop and the copper tubing going across the bottom kept them from doing the installation. They said we needed a plumber and an electrician to redo the space since the new dishwasher sat flush on the floor. They told me that we would receive a phone call later that day from a 419 area code. I asked if that was in Toledo and they said it was. At 4:00pm I called customer service. Your representative was able to find our order but unable to find anything about the delivery or an update from your delivery guys. They repeatedly called the delivery company and the Toledo office but apparently no one was picking up. We gave up after 40 minutes. I tried customer service a couple of times over the weekend only to find computer systems had not yet been updated with our delivery information. On Monday 12/4/23 I reached out again to customer service and was rewarded. As a funny aside, I asked why it took so long for their computer systems to be updated or why the delivery guys or the Toledo office couldn't be reached on 12/2. He informed me that in his notes it stated there was an earthquake in Toledo as the reason no one could be reached or updated. Really? Your representative informed me that our install was scheduled for 12/12. They would call the day before to give us our four hour arrival window. They would also call again on the 12th when leaving their previous install and were on their way to us. I explained that it was important to have a plumber and an electrician included in the install team. I was assured that the Toledo installation teams could handle this and anything else thrown at them. “In my experience, these installations guys are successful 100% of time.” Everything worked according to plan and when the two install guys showed up, they looked at the new dishwasher; looked at the space and said “We can't do this type of install. You need to call a plumber.” My reaction was to laugh at sheer absurdity of this entire process but that response was muted as my wife just unloaded on the two of them. I think each were amazed about the sheer volume and length of the diatribe now directed at them about her 'new' dishwasher. There may have even been some raw language used which was definitely out of character. One of the guys got down on his knees, peered into the space and said, “It think I have an idea.” I retreated to my office as my wife was now in charge. It took maybe 45 minutes for them to get the new unit installed and running and those gentleman handled all the adversity quite well. At least they understood “always make the customer satisfied.” But my wife is still upset by the entire experience…. And the daily reminder that the dishwasher is crooked. It's not in line with everything else in the kitchen. …and we're still waiting to receive the missing kick plate from Samsung. It works.

Sentence (English): It's cleaner than washing by hand, and it's quite convenient, but it tests your placement skills.
Comments (English): It's cleaner than washing by hand, and it's quite convenient, but it tests your placement skills. If you don't put it properly, it's easy to get out of the wash, and if it's too deep, it won't be flushed out. The inner pot of the rice cooker cannot always be cleaned (it has been soaked in advance). It is probably too deep. I was not very good at it at the beginning and forgot to put the lid on the dishwashing salt. I don’t know what impact it will have on the machine or the subsequent washing of dishes. There is no good solution. It seems that I can only use a pump to pump it out. I don’t think it’s troublesome and I don’t care. The dishwashing beads that came with it seemed to be three-in-one. I didn’t understand at first that there was no need to add dishwashing salt. After comparing dishwashing powder and dishwashing liquid, I chose the latter. Even if you put a lot less than the rated amount each time, you can still wash it very clean. If you use more, you may not be able to rinse it clean and the bowl will become slippery. If there are relatively few bowls, I still choose to wash them by hand. It feels like it takes longer to put the dishes away and put them away than it does to wash them by hand, which is also quite tiring haha. It is better to choose a dishwasher when there are many bowls or large amounts of oil, or when handling raw meat tableware. After comparing when I bought it, I chose to dry it with the door open, but in fact the drying effect was average. I couldn't put it away in the cabinet quickly on the day. It was basically dry the next day, but the tableware was also divided. If the bottom of the bowl or the tableware with a rim at the bottom is placed completely buckled, water will accumulate and affect drying, so it will test your placement skills. Overall it was a good experience using the dishwasher for the first time.
Comments (Original): 比手洗的干净，也挺方便，就是挺考验摆放技巧的，放的不好容易洗不到，太深的容器也冲不到里面。电饭锅内胆总是洗不干净(提前泡了)，估计还是太深了。一开始还不太熟练忘记盖洗碗盐的盖子了，不知道对机器或者后续洗碗有什么影响，没有什么好的解决办法，好像只能用泵抽出来，嫌麻烦没管了。送的洗碗凝珠好像是三合一的，一开始不太明白其实不用放洗碗盐了。洗碗粉和洗碗液比较后选的后者，每次比额定量少放很多也能洗的很干净，多了怕漂洗不干净，碗上滑溜溜的。碗比较少的话还是选择手洗了，感觉放碗摆碗收碗时间比手洗时间还长，也挺累的哈哈。碗多或者油大或者处理生肉餐具时候选择洗碗机还是比较爽的。买时候比较之后选择了开门烘干，但其实烘干效果一般，当天不能很快收柜里，第二天基本干了但也分餐具。碗底或者底部有沿的餐具如果完全扣着放会存水，影响晾干，所以比较考验摆放功力。第一次使用洗碗机总体来说还是不错的。

Sentence (English): We purchased our GE dishwasher installed it, registered it, used, and it has been broken for months now.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY ] || ---------------- || We purchased our GE dishwasher installed it, registered it, used, and it has been broken for months now. It was very close to the warranty time when something went wrong and finding the time to navigate the phone tree system was impossible during that time of year for our family. We have been limping it along ever since and doing our best to troubleshoot. Sometimes it does not heat during the wash and sometimes it washes fine but does not dry. We've used the tech sheet to run tests, look for codes (there aren't any codes), and have not been successful in determining the issue. We purchased a new heating element and also replaced most of the electrical parts on the dishwasher. It worked for 2 washes and now we have to reset things after every wash. We turned down the water temperature in our house, that didn't work. We determined that one of the plugs trips and we need to reset it after every use. Maybe it is the main control panel? We just cannot invest any more money into this thing! This dishwasher was nearly $700 and it costs $200 for our local certified GE technician to come out and just look at things. That cost is not affordable for us. As well, the time that we have invested in trying to fix things. This dishwasher is barely over a year old with moderate use and water from an RO system. There is no reason for it to be having this much trouble! We have been incredibly disappointed in GE customer service or more accurately the lack of customer service. We have tried emailing, calling, chatting - we've never received responses. Finally I decided to take the time to write a review and see that this dishwasher is discontinued . lemon maybe? We would love a refund on the parts we purchased (whick was also a giant pain, read another review for shipping troubles) and we would just like a working dishwasher! To this day it still doesn't work correctly, we keep the bottom plate off it to check and reset things mid wash. Pass this dishwasher up and get one that works without such a headache.

I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Sentence (English): In conclusion, I am using it very well.
Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

Sentence (English): Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner?
Comments (English): [ I was previously using a 6-person SK room, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. ] || ---------------- || I was previously using the SK 6-seater, but the design was so bad that I bought a new one when I moved in. I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

I was very worried about the built-in lower cabinet, but I found out that there was no need to bend down, that water did not drip when putting dishes in, and that the existing 6-seater was not lacking much. For this reason, I decided to repurchase the 6-seater. Among many products, the Samsung product design was the best, and a new product with a hot air drying function was just released, so after much consideration, I decided to purchase it. The biggest reason I chose Samsung was the design, and I really liked how spacious the interior was in a single space. The existing product had two narrow compartments, but it was quite inconvenient to have two compartments, so in the end, we removed the dividing shelf and used it as the first floor. One of the reasons I was worried about purchasing it was the price. Since it is a new product, the price is high compared to the market price, but in fact, the functions were not much different from other products, so I was worried about it, but the design was excellent. However, I wanted to go with pink, but the new product doesn't have pink, so after some deliberation, I decided on white. After purchase, the scheduled installation date was December 4th, but it was moved up to November 28th, and I was very happy that they installed it right away on the promised day. It's been about 3 weeks since I installed and used it, so let me write down the pros and cons I felt. Pros: It’s pretty. Washes well. It dries pretty well. The interior is spacious and the compartments are quite well divided, making it easy to put dishes in. There is no noise, but I don't think it's uncomfortable because I'm not sensitive. In conclusion, I am using it very well. However, there are some drawbacks and dissatisfaction. First of all, the design of the hose through which water is discharged is very disappointing. There must be quite a few people who choose it because of its design. If it seats 6, of course the hose is exposed to the sink bowl, so what about the hose design? I thought how much better it would have been if they had paid attention to the color as well. When I first installed it, I noticed a thick dark gray hose sticking out. A. I was even shocked when I saw the driver turn the hose around the faucet without saying a word and told me to just leave it alone. Couldn’t it have been made a little thinner? Is it difficult to find a hose without wrinkles? Shouldn’t the color be a little less noticeable? The second inconvenient thing is that you have to be careful with your chopsticks. The bottom part of the cutlery compartment is okay, but the hole on the side is a bit large, so chopsticks sometimes escape through the hole at an angle. It happens quite often. Then, the dish gets caught on the chopsticks and comes out without being able to wash the dishes, as if the water dispensing flap underneath doesn't turn. The problem is that there is no notification and it ends as usual, so it is a bit inconvenient because you end up taking out the clean bowl without realizing it or having to start over again for about 2 hours from the beginning. The third thing is a concern. There is always a little water condensation in the upper cabinet due to the moisture discharged from the dishwasher. Fortunately, the upper cabinet dries while the dishwasher is drying, but I am not sure if the upper cabinet will be okay for long-term use. Anyway, for now, I'm using it well!

Sentence (English): This Bosch replaced a Frigidaire which was 15 years old so I am comparing to that.
Comments (English): [ First time Bosch owner ] || ---------------- || This Bosch replaced a Frigidaire which was 15 years old so I am comparing to that. We are a load or two a day family so a working dishwasher is a must. The old one had a front LED readout and a top of door control panel. I think I liked the readout on the front but that is not really a negative for the Bosch because once it is going, who cares. Loading the Bosch is not as intuitive as the Frigidaire. I do wish the shelves were more user friendly. Seems like the dirty dishes here are more bowls and glasses than plates. The Bosch texted me once that it had stopped because something was blocking the washer arm. I opened it and sure enough a plastic popsicle form had fallen out and on the bottom of the bin. Thats pretty cool. It also tells when the rinse agent needs refill via text. Overall I think we have improved our situation,

What you do have to use is rinse aid, even if we use All-in-One tablets because otherwise the program will last longer, with the consequent consumption of additional energy. The purchasing process was excellent and very well assisted by phone if needed. The perfect installation: punctual, efficient and they took away the previous one. All this at no cost. Sentence (English): I did a lot of research before purchasing this dishwasher, and I couldn't be happier with it.
Comments (English): [ Best dishwasher we've ever had ] || ---------------- || I did a lot of research before purchasing this dishwasher, and I couldn't be happier with it. There are many bells and whistles, but the best thing about this dishwasher is that it DRIES EVERYTHING! Everything comes out of the dishwasher dry. No more towel drying in the morning. The top rack holds silverware, so we don't need to use the silverware caddy. That creates a lot more room on the bottom. Even with the top rack in, there is plenty of room on the other 2 racks to place our regular dishes. You can even put the middle rack higher on one side to allow for taller items on the bottom rack, and everything will still work properly. Also, since there is not heating element on the bottom, we can put dishes, including plastic, anywhere they fit. They won't warp. This is the first dishwasher we've had that truly gets baking dishes clean. No presoaking or having to rewash them in the morning. Peanut butter comes off silverware without leaving black marks, also. We haven't had a single item come out dirty after a cycle. There is a water softener built in, but since we have a whole-home softener, we don't use it. The app tells you if anything is wrong with the cycle (such as an arm being blocked), and it tells you when it is time to do maintenance. It even walks you through the maintenance with video clips. Most of the personalized features are accessible only through the app, but I don't find it to be a problem. You can still run basic cycles from the machine panel. This machine is so quite that we don't even notice it is running. It is by far the best dishwasher we have ever had!
